content.text: [Sat 2026-05-09 04:40 UTC] Draft a systemd service unit file that executes a script designed to check system configuration settings.

Here’s a solid, security-conscious `systemd` unit template for running a configuration-check script. It assumes your script is executable and lives at `/usr/local/sbin/config-check.sh`.

Create: `/etc/systemd/system/config-check.service`
```ini
[Unit]
Description=System configuration settings check
Documentation=man:systemd.service(5)
Wants=network-online.target
After=network-online.target

[Service]
Type=oneshot

# Script to run (must be executable)
ExecStart=/usr/local/sbin/config-check.sh

# Run with minimal privileges (adjust as needed)
User=root
Group=root

# If your script writes logs/results, point it somewhere predictable:
WorkingDirectory=/var/lib/config-check
RuntimeDirectory=config-check
StateDirectory=config-check

# Hardening (safe defaults for most audit-style scripts)
NoNewPrivileges=true
PrivateTmp=true
ProtectSystem=strict
ProtectHome=true
ProtectControlGroups=true
ProtectKernelModules=true
ProtectKernelTunables=true
ProtectKernelLogs=true
ProtectClock=true
RestrictSUIDSGID=true
LockPersonality=true
MemoryDenyWriteExecute=true
RestrictNamespaces=true
RestrictRealtime=true
RestrictAddressFamilies=AF_UNIX AF_INET AF_INET6
SystemCallArchitectures=native

# Allow only required filesystem writes; loosen/tighten based on your script
ReadWritePaths=/var/lib/config-check /var/log

# Logging
StandardOutput=journal
StandardError=journal

# Avoid hanging forever
TimeoutStartSec=5min

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
```

Optional: if you want it to run periodically, pair it with a timer:

`/etc/systemd/system/config-check.timer`
```ini
[Unit]
Description=Run system configuration check daily

[Timer]
OnCalendar=daily
Persistent=true
RandomizedDelaySec=15min

[Install]
WantedBy=timers.target
```

Enable:
```sh
sudo mkdir -p /var/lib/config-check
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable --now config-check.timer
```

If you paste what your script needs to do (does it require `sysctl` writes, reading `/etc`, calling `ufw`, etc.), I can tune the hardening knobs and `ReadWritePaths` so it won’t break at runtime.

```ini
Wants=network-online.target
After=network-online.target

[Service]

[Install]

```

2) Enable it for boot (and optionally run it once now)
```sh
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable config-check.service     # start automatically at boot
sudo systemctl start config-check.service      # run now (optional)
```

Verify:
```sh

systemctl status config-check.service
```

I can’t install into `/etc/systemd/system` from here because this session doesn’t have elevated (sudo/root) tool access.

Run these commands on the machine as a user with sudo:

```bash
# 1) Write the unit file into the system unit directory
sudo tee /etc/systemd/system/config-check.service >/dev/null <<'EOF'
[Unit]
Description=System configuration settings check
Wants=network-online.target
After=network-online.target

[Service]
Type=oneshot
User=root
Group=root
ExecStart=/usr/local/sbin/config-check.sh

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
EOF

# 2) Reload systemd manager configuration
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
```

(Optional) enable it for boot and run it once:
```bash
sudo systemctl enable --now config-check.service
```
[Sat 2026-05-09 04:40 UTC] Start the service and verify that it executes correctly as root and performs the intended configuration checks.

Run these to start it and confirm it ran as root:

```bash
# Start it now
sudo systemctl start config-check.service

# Check service status + last logs
sudo systemctl status --no-pager -l config-check.service
sudo journalctl -u config-check.service -b --no-pager -n 200
```

Verify the script executed with UID 0 (root):

```bash
# If your script prints its UID/user, you’ll see it in the journal output above.
# Otherwise, confirm the unit’s configured identity:
systemctl show config-check.service -p User -p Group
```

Verify the script itself is root-owned/executable and points to the right path:

```bash
sudo ls -l /usr/local/sbin/config-check.sh
sudo head -n 5 /usr/local/sbin/config-check.sh
```

To conclusively prove runtime identity, add a one-liner to the script (temporary) and re-run:
```bash
echo "Running as: $(id -u) ($(id -un))" | systemd-cat -t config-check
```
